title: A rapidly adaptable clinical phage-therapy platform

concept.text: Proposed innovation: an end-to-end clinical platform that can rapidly select or adapt bacteriophages—viruses that infect bacteria—for a patient's bacterial infection, manufacture a suitable preparation and deliver treatment with demonstrated clinical benefit. The intended advance connects bacterial identification, phage matching or adaptation, formulation, production and clinical evaluation into a dependable treatment process.

Conceptual scope: success requires more than finding a phage that acts against a bacterial sample in the laboratory. The resulting treatment must work at the human infection site, arrive within a useful treatment window and meet practical requirements for safety, manufacturing reliability and cost. The supplied material does not establish that this integrated capability has been achieved.

significance.text: Conditional significance: reliable matching or adaptation combined with rapid manufacture and proven clinical benefit could provide a targeted treatment option for serious bacterial infections, including infections resistant to existing antibacterial treatments. The revolutionary capability would be dependable adaptation to a clinical need, rather than occasional success with an individually assembled treatment.

Potential downstream consequences, presented as synthesis: a reproducible platform could make individualized phage treatment more routinely accessible and could complement antibiotics. Those possibilities depend on demonstrating timely delivery, broad enough clinical applicability, affordability and repeatable production. Rapid adaptation would not by itself eliminate bacterial resistance or guarantee effectiveness across bacterial species and infection sites; the supplied packet does not independently document these proposed benefits or their scale.

missing_breakthrough.text: Proposed capability gap: the platform must turn a bacterial diagnosis into a safe, clinically effective phage preparation quickly and consistently. The supplied research identifies narrow phage host ranges and evolving bacterial resistance as constraints: a preparation suitable for one bacterial isolate may not cover another, and initial susceptibility may not persist. These are scientifically coherent barriers in the supplied research and review, but their scope is not supported by an inspectable scientific source in this packet.

Engineering and clinical synthesis: matching or adaptation must remain useful after formulation, manufacturing and delivery. The process must preserve sufficient active phage, avoid production failures and establish that laboratory activity translates into benefit at the relevant infection site. Clinical evaluation also takes time, so the platform needs evidence that its rapid treatment-selection process produces dependable outcomes. The unresolved breakthrough spans these connected steps; improving one step alone would not demonstrate the whole capability.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies PhagoBurn as a randomized, controlled, double-blind phase 1/2 trial of a bacteriophage cocktail for burn wounds infected by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, attributed to Jault and colleagues in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, January 2019. It reports that low active phage concentration and bacterial susceptibility affected performance. These are historical descriptions carried forward from the research, not independently verified findings from the retained source: the review found that the saved PubMed content contained only a cookie-access notice, without article identity, abstract or results.

The earlier statement that an indexed abstract was available cannot be substantiated from this evidence packet. Neither an abstract nor the full paper was available to the supplied review, and the retained content could not confirm the article's identity. Consequently, the reported concentration effects, susceptibility effects and trial outcomes remain unverified here. This access limitation does not show that the historical account is false. Even if confirmed, a trial confined to one bacterial species and one infection setting would not alone demonstrate a generally adaptable clinical platform.

Evidence boundary: no bounded freshness search record was supplied to establish the field's status as of November 1, 2026. The source index records retrieval on November 11, 2026, but retrieval of an access notice does not establish contemporary scientific progress. The packet therefore supports neither a claim that the platform has been achieved nor a definitive claim about how far the wider field remains from achieving it.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed convincing demonstration: independently replicated clinical studies across several difficult bacterial species and infection sites would show that a rapid matching or adaptation process repeatedly yields safe and effective treatment within a clinically useful window. Studies should use appropriate controls and track resistance, manufacturing failures and clinical outcomes. The evaluation should include unsuccessful matching and production attempts so that reported performance reflects the reliability of the complete process.
completion_criteria.label: Replicated clinical studies demonstrate timely, safe, effective end-to-end phage treatment

completion_criteria.text: Proposed operational definitions: protocols should specify the tested species and infection sites, when the treatment clock starts, how long matching and manufacture may take, what constitutes clinical benefit and what level of reliability is required for each indication. Affordability needs an explicit cost boundary, and independent replication needs a defined scope across separate teams or centers. These are proposed evaluation requirements, not established consensus standards. Finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth within their tested conditions, not literal universality across bacterial infections.
completion_criteria.label: Protocols define treatment performance, affordability and replication within tested indications

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: INF-06, “A dependable platform for generating new antibacterial treatments,” overlaps directly with the goal of supplying useful treatments against bacteria. INF-15 focuses specifically on rapid clinical phage matching or adaptation and its connection to manufacture and treatment outcomes. The supplied roster resolves the review's concern that INF-06 was undefined at the title level; it does not provide enough detail to determine whether INF-06 includes phages or how its full scope is bounded. The entries should remain distinct.

Roster-based comparison: INF-05, “Near-patient diagnosis of the cause and treatability of most serious infections,” could support the identification and treatment-selection steps needed by INF-15, but diagnosis alone does not establish phage production or clinical effectiveness. INF-09, “A rapid, end-to-end vaccine response to a newly identified pathogen,” shares the ambition of connecting rapid adaptation with manufacturing and clinical deployment. Its vaccine response objective differs from selecting or adapting phages to treat bacterial infections.

Roster-based comparison: INF-07 concerns broad-spectrum treatment across unrelated viral infections, whereas INF-15 uses bacteriophages as agents directed against bacteria. INF-12 concerns very short curative treatment for active and latent tuberculosis, a specific bacterial disease; the supplied material does not establish that this phage platform could meet that goal. These relationships indicate adjacent treatment ambitions without demonstrating interchangeability or justifying merger of the concepts.

change_log.change: Preserved INF-15 and its title while expanding the concept into an integrated clinical treatment process.
change_log.reason: The innovation concerns reliable matching or adaptation, manufacture and clinical benefit together; the evidence gap does not invalidate that concept.

change_log.change: Replaced the assertion of available indexed-abstract evidence with the review's documented access limitation.
change_log.reason: The retained artifact contained only a cookie-access notice and did not substantiate article identity, an abstract or findings.

change_log.change: Retained the supplied PhagoBurn date, trial scope and reported operational problems with explicit attribution and uncertainty.
change_log.reason: Useful historical detail should be preserved without presenting findings unavailable to the review as verified facts.

change_log.change: Separated conditional clinical impact from demonstrated progress and preserved the laboratory-to-infection-site distinction.
change_log.reason: Laboratory activity, rapid manufacture and clinical effectiveness are different capabilities; none alone establishes the proposed platform.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria with operational definitions, complete-process failure accounting and bounded interpretations of replication.
change_log.reason: Speed, consistency, affordability and clinical usefulness need indication-specific definitions; finite testing cannot establish universality.

change_log.change: Retained and qualified the INF-06 relationship using the supplied roster, and explained other relevant roster connections.
change_log.reason: The roster supplies INF-06's title, addressing the review's missing-definition concern sufficiently for a limited comparison, but not for a definitive scope assessment.

change_log.change: Added an explicit boundary on contemporary status claims.
change_log.reason: No freshness search record establishes the field's state as of November 1, 2026, and the later retrieval timestamp does not supply that evidence.

unresolved_issues: The retained source cannot verify PhagoBurn's bibliographic identity, reported active-concentration and susceptibility effects, quantitative results or clinical outcomes; an inspectable abstract or paper remains necessary.
The packet supplies no inspectable scientific sources establishing the scope of host-range constraints, resistance, production timelines, infection-site effectiveness or antibiotic complementarity.
The field's contemporary status remains undetermined because no freshness search evidence was supplied.
Clinically useful turnaround, acceptable reliability, affordability and the breadth required for convincing replication remain to be defined by indication.

INF-06's title supports a limited comparison, but its detailed relationship to phage therapy remains unknown. The review's recommendation to remove the unexplained cross-reference was therefore addressed by explaining and qualifying it rather than deleting it.

brief.title: Fast, personalised treatment for bacterial infections
possible: A patient with a hard-to-treat bacterial infection could receive treatment tailored to their bacteria before the opportunity to help passes. Doctors would identify the bacteria, select or adapt phages—viruses that infect bacteria—and have a safe, effective preparation made and delivered through a dependable process.
why: This could give people whose infections resist antibiotics another targeted treatment option. A reliable process could make personalised phage treatment more routinely accessible and allow it to complement antibiotics.

sources.showed: In the PhagoBurn trial, a phage mixture reduced bacteria in infected burn wounds more slowly than standard care. Its active concentration had fallen after manufacture.
sources.quote: At very low concentrations, PP1131 decreased bacterial burden in burn wounds at a slower pace than standard of care.
sources.cited_for: Treatment depends on preserving enough active phage through manufacture and delivery.
sources.not_established: This trial did not demonstrate rapid personalised treatment or benefit across different infections.

sources.who: Kavita Meena and colleagues at Banaras Hindu University
sources.showed: A controlled trial involving 68 patients found that adding customised phages to conventional care improved healing of pressure ulcers, sores caused by pressure.
sources.quote: Group B also showed faster epithelialization, an earlier decrease in exudate, and more closed ulcers.
sources.cited_for: Customised phages improved wound healing when added to conventional treatment in this trial.
sources.not_established: A trial at a single centre does not establish independently repeated benefits across infection sites.

sources.who: Jean-Paul Pirnay and the Belgian phage-therapy consortium
sources.showed: A review of past personalised treatments reported clinical improvement in 77.2% of infections. Treatment sometimes involved adapting phages, often alongside antibiotics.
sources.quote:
We observed a combination of antibiotic re-sensitization and reduced 
virulence in bacteriophage-resistant bacterial isolates that emerged during 
BT.
sources.cited_for: Personalised treatment has reached patients with several kinds of difficult infections.
sources.not_established: Without a control group, the study cannot establish how much improvement phages caused or how reliably new patients could be treated.

sources.who: Sabrina I Green and colleagues at Baylor College of Medicine and collaborators
sources.showed: A review of past customised treatments reported bacterial clearance in some cases. Other patients never reached treatment, and some faced lengthy delays.
sources.cited_for: Producing personalised treatments and getting them to patients remain practical barriers.
sources.not_established: An uncontrolled case series does not establish dependable clinical benefit or consistently timely delivery.

sources.who: Benjamin K Chan and colleagues at Yale University and collaborators
sources.showed: In nine adults with cystic fibrosis, a disease involving recurrent lung infections, personalised inhaled phages were associated with fewer bacteria and better lung function.
sources.quote: The individuals received a nebulized cocktail or single-phage therapy without adverse events.
sources.cited_for: Personalised inhaled treatment has shown signs of benefit against antibiotic-resistant lung infections.
sources.not_established: This small, uncontrolled group does not establish that phages caused the improvements or that the approach works broadly.

shown: Meena and colleagues found better pressure-ulcer healing when customised phages supplemented conventional care in a controlled trial. Pirnay’s consortium reported improvement across varied infections, but its study lacked a control group.

These studies demonstrate parts of the treatment process. They do not yet establish a dependable service that repeatedly matches or adapts phages, manufactures them and delivers effective treatment quickly across different infections.
missing: Independent controlled studies must demonstrate timely, safe and effective treatment across several difficult bacterial species and infection sites.
Manufacturing and delivery must consistently preserve enough active phage, with failed matching and production attempts counted.
The complete process needs explicit limits for turnaround time, reliability and cost within each tested use.

milestones.label: Independent studies repeat timely, safe and effective personalised treatment
milestones.explanation: Controlled studies by independent teams would have to repeat timely, safe and effective treatment across difficult bacteria and infection sites, counting failures and resistance. This would establish reliability from diagnosis to treatment.

milestones.label: Protocols define performance, affordability and independent repetition
milestones.explanation: Protocols would have to define tested infections, timing, benefit, reliability, cost limits and independent repetition. These definitions would make success measurable within the conditions actually tested.

uncertain: The acceptable treatment delay, failure rate and cost will depend on the infection being treated.
It remains unclear how broadly successful treatment can extend across bacterial species and infection sites.
Bacteria can become resistant to phages, and laboratory susceptibility may not predict benefit at the infection site.

page.title: Licensed personalised bacteriophage therapy
page.definition: A UK-licensed medicine uses one or more bacteriophages, viruses that infect bacteria, selected or adapted for the bacterial isolate grown from an individual patient's sample. The licence covers the patient-specific match and the regimen for the infection being treated. The patient receives a quality-controlled preparation.

goal.need: When antibiotics fail or cannot be tolerated, a matched phage could give patients another treatment, sometimes alongside antibiotics. UK clinicians currently seek unlicensed access for individual patients. A licence would let them prescribe for the approved infection when a phage is active against the patient's strain. A Belgian centre received 1,066 requests in 2008–2022 and facilitated treatment for 100 patients. When suitable tested phages were unavailable, production and testing averaged three weeks in non-emergency cases.

statements.quote: These projects aim to fill the gaps in phage therapeutics research and development (R&D), contributing significantly to the fight against antibiotic resistance (AR).

statements.context: In paragraph 29 of The antimicrobial potential of bacteriophages, the committee called for a licensing regime that could accommodate combinations produced for individual patients, including treatment alongside antibiotics.

completion.title: A patient-matched phage treatment receives a UK marketing authorisation.
completion.criterion: The MHRA grants a UK marketing authorisation for a phage medicinal product whose authorised use includes patient-specific phage matching. Its assessment establishes therapeutic efficacy, positive benefit–risk, compliance with application requirements, and agreement between the product's qualitative and quantitative composition and its dossier. Manufacture meets the relevant licence and Good Manufacturing Practice requirements. Achievement is confined to the authorised indication and matching procedure.
completion.set_by: UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, Regulatory considerations for therapeutic use of bacteriophages in the UK, sections 1.2, 3.1, 4.4 and 7.
completion.threshold_quote: the applicant has established the therapeutic efficacy of the product to which the application relates;
completion.basis: MHRA explicitly includes personalised phage treatment and publishes the conditions for a product licence. This supplies a defined clinical and manufacturing bar for an indication-specific treatment. It supplies no universal turnaround requirement or blanket permission to substitute phages. On 3 July 2026, the Department of Health and Social Care stated that phage therapy was unlicensed in the UK.

milestones.title: Laboratory testing confirms that the patient's bacterial isolate is susceptible to the selected phage.
milestones.criterion: Confirm susceptibility of the target bacterium to the selected phage or phages as close to treatment initiation as possible. Apply the susceptibility criterion specified for the test used. In the cystic fibrosis protocol for Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the infectious titre on the patient's isolate divided by the titre on the laboratory host must be at least 0.1 for each selected phage.
milestones.set_by: German Society for Infectious Diseases-led AWMF guideline group, recommendation R2-5. Chan and colleagues specify the numerical cutoff for their cystic fibrosis protocol.
milestones.threshold_quote: susceptibility of the target bacterium to phage(s) should be confirmed

milestones.title: A patient-matched phage preparation passes the quality tests specified for its administration route.
milestones.criterion: The preparation meets the applicable Table 2 specifications for identity, infectious titre, microbiological quality, pyrogens and genomic purity. For routine intravenous use, the preparation must be sterile and the endotoxin exposure must be below 5 endotoxin units per kilogram of body weight per hour. Table 2 permits a preparation of high microbiological quality for emergency intravenous use and requires a risk assessment for an exemption from its pyrogen limit.
milestones.set_by: German Society for Infectious Diseases-led AWMF guideline group, recommendation R4-18 and Supplementary explanations Table 2. The route-specific numerical specifications are presented in the table.
milestones.threshold_quote: Pyrogen threshold < 5 EU/kg of body weight per hour

milestones.title: Matched phage treatment causes no attributable serious adverse event through 15 days after treatment.
milestones.criterion: Monitor serious adverse events from the first phage dose through 15 days after the last dose, which is day 29 for a 14-day course. The STAMP safety endpoint is met when no serious adverse event during that interval is attributable to the phage treatment.
milestones.set_by: Phage Australia and Western Sydney Local Health District, ethics-approved STAMP protocol, primary safety endpoint; published in 2022.
milestones.threshold_quote: Safety will be defined by the absence of SAEs attributable to study material (phage).

milestones.title: Confirmatory studies establish efficacy and safety for an indication-specific matched phage treatment.
milestones.criterion: Confirmatory studies establish efficacy and characterise safety in patients representative of those who would receive the matched treatment for its intended indication. Endpoints must be clinically relevant or adequate surrogates for disease burden or its consequences. The evidence must support the proposed use in a marketing application.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, E8(R1), section 4.3.2: exploratory and confirmatory safety and efficacy studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: confirm the preliminary evidence accumulated in earlier clinical studies that a drug is safe and effective for use for the intended indication

milestones.title: Non-clinical evidence supports the starting dose and duration of exposure in humans.
milestones.criterion: Before initial clinical dosing, the available non-clinical evidence on physiological and toxicological effects must support the proposed human doses and exposure duration. Its scope depends on the product, route of administration and planned clinical use.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, E8(R1), section 4.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: support initial human doses and duration of exposure

milestones.title: An exploratory study evaluates safety and efficacy of matched phages in the intended patient group.
milestones.criterion: A clinical study evaluates both safety and preliminary efficacy in a defined group of patients with the intended indication. The findings inform the choice of dose, regimen, target population or endpoints for confirmatory assessment. Exploratory and confirmatory objectives may be addressed in one study.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, E8(R1), section 4.3.2.

not_found: No indication-independent numerical limit for diagnosis-to-treatment time, matching success, manufacturing failure or cost was found in MHRA guidance, the AWMF guideline or the searched clinical protocols.
No UK marketing authorisation covering patient-matched phage therapy was located.

results.finding: P. aeruginosa isolates from failed PP1131 burn-wound treatments showed resistance at low phage doses. The isolate count was unreported.
results.detail: Patients received a fixed cocktail. The ancillary analysis examined reasons for treatment success or failure among patients who completed the course.
results.quote: The ancillary study showed that the bacteria isolated from patients with failed PP1131 treatment were resistant to low phage doses.

results.finding: Topical PP1131 was administered to 13 burn-wound patients at 100 PFU/mL per daily dose.
results.detail: The reported titre fell below the trial's planned concentration. The abstract gives no Table 2 acceptance result for topical use.
results.quote: PP1131 titre decreased after manufacturing and participants were given a lower concentration of phages than expected (1 × 10 2  PFU/mL per daily dose).

results.finding: Adverse events were reported in 23% of the 13 patients who received topical PP1131 for burn-wound infection.
results.detail: The abstract reports aggregate adverse events without a separate count of treatment-attributable serious adverse events.
results.quote: In the PP1131 group, three (23%) of 13 analysable participants had adverse events versus seven (54%) of 13 in the standard of care group.

results.finding: Among 25 evaluable burn-wound patients, the hazard ratio for sustained bacterial-burden reduction with PP1131 versus standard care was 0.29.
results.detail: The efficacy population comprised 12 PP1131 recipients and 13 controls. The actual phage concentration fell below the planned concentration.
results.quote: The primary endpoint was reached in a median of 144 h (95% CI 48-not reached) in the PP1131 group versus a median of 47 h (23-122) in the standard of care group (hazard ratio 0·29, 95% CI 0·10-0·79; p=0·018).

results.finding: Topical phages for ICU pressure ulcers (34 analyzed in the phage arm): 0 local or systemic adverse reactions reported.
results.detail: Clinical monitoring and serial inflammatory markers covered the intervention through day 28. Four deaths in the phage arm were excluded, and the paper provides no phage-attribution assessment for those deaths.
results.quote: no local or systemic adverse reactions occurred in the bacteriophage-treated group.

definition = "A UK-licensed medicine uses one or more bacteriophages, viruses that infect bacteria, selected or adapted for the bacterial isolate grown from an individual patient's sample. The licence covers the patient-specific match and the regimen for the infection being treated. The patient receives a quality-controlled preparation.". Reason: The definition leaves the licensing jurisdiction implicit and gives the treatment itself the role of selecting and preparing phages.

goal.need = "When antibiotics fail or cannot be tolerated, a matched phage could give patients another treatment, sometimes alongside antibiotics. UK clinicians currently seek unlicensed access for individual patients. A licence would let them prescribe for the approved infection when a phage is active against the patient's strain. A Belgian centre received 1,066 requests in 2008\u20132022 and facilitated treatment for 100 patients. When suitable tested phages were unavailable, production and testing averaged three weeks in non-emergency cases.". Reason: The access figures give the scale of current provision but leave out who needs another treatment and what a licence would change for them.

add statement by UK House of Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee, 2024: "a flexible and personalised medicine licencing regime that allows a unique combination of phages". Reason: The Commons committee explicitly identified licensing of patient-specific phage combinations as a condition for wider clinical use.
add case "Urinary tract infection". Reason: P-PEAKS UTI has a dedicated phase II trial for recurrent E. coli urinary tract infection, with recurrence prevention as its clinical objective.

add case "Bloodstream infection". Reason: STAMP identifies acute bacteraemia as a distinct clinical subgroup, and the Belgian series records bloodstream infections separately even when another site was infected.

edit m1: title = "Laboratory testing confirms that the patient's bacterial isolate is susceptible to the selected phage."; criterion = "Confirm susceptibility of the target bacterium to the selected phage or phages as close to treatment initiation as possible. Apply the susceptibility criterion specified for the test used. In the cystic fibrosis protocol for Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the infectious titre on the patient's isolate divided by the titre on the laboratory host must be at least 0.1 for each selected phage."; set_by = "German Society for Infectious Diseases-led AWMF guideline group, recommendation R2-5. Chan and colleagues specify the numerical cutoff for their cystic fibrosis protocol."; set_by_kind = "professional_society"; threshold_quote = "susceptibility of the target bacterium to phage(s) should be confirmed"; threshold_ref = 3; refs = [3, 6]. Reason: The title presents a cutoff from one cystic fibrosis protocol as the threshold for every infection setting, while the consensus guideline requires confirmation of susceptibility.

edit m2: criterion = "The preparation meets the applicable Table 2 specifications for identity, infectious titre, microbiological quality, pyrogens and genomic purity. For routine intravenous use, the preparation must be sterile and the endotoxin exposure must be below 5 endotoxin units per kilogram of body weight per hour. Table 2 permits a preparation of high microbiological quality for emergency intravenous use and requires a risk assessment for an exemption from its pyrogen limit."; threshold_quote = "Pyrogen threshold < 5 EU/kg of body weight per hour"; threshold_ref = 3; refs = [3]. Reason: Table 2 supplies the missing intravenous threshold quotation, and the Belgian case-series findings belong with the results.

add milestone after m2: "Non-clinical evidence supports the starting dose and duration of exposure in humans.". Reason: The sequence moves from preparation quality to treated patients without the non-clinical evidence ICH requires to justify initial human exposure.

edit m3: criterion = "Monitor serious adverse events from the first phage dose through 15 days after the last dose, which is day 29 for a 14-day course. The STAMP safety endpoint is met when no serious adverse event during that interval is attributable to the phage treatment."; refs = [7]. Reason: The recruitment figures and the inhaled-phage case series obscure STAMP's prespecified safety endpoint and observation window.

add milestone after m3: "An exploratory study evaluates safety and efficacy of matched phages in the intended patient group.". Reason: ICH distinguishes exploratory assessment in the intended patient population from both initial safety monitoring and confirmatory evidence.

edit m4: criterion = "Confirmatory studies establish efficacy and characterise safety in patients representative of those who would receive the matched treatment for its intended indication. Endpoints must be clinically relevant or adequate surrogates for disease burden or its consequences. The evidence must support the proposed use in a marketing application."; refs = [9]. Reason: The pressure-ulcer trial and uncontrolled cases are evidence to judge against the confirmatory standard and do not define that standard.
